newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P says Australasian securitisation booming.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Australasian securitisation booming.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Thursday it has assigned ratings to A$6.2 billion of securitisation and commerical paper programmes in the Australasian capital markets in the first six months of 1997 of which A$5.0 billion of debt was actually issued.
This represents a 94.90 percent increase in new ratings over the same period in 1996, more than 2.5 times the amount of debt actually issued, it said.
In the six months to 1997, it rated 16 new programmes in the Australasian market, an increase of 33 percent on the number of new programmes rated during the same period in 1996.

S&P said the mortgage-backed sector remained the strongest during the year to date, making up 64 percent of new programmes rated and reflected the success of non-bank originators were achievng in the home loan market.
These account for 54.2 percent of new ratings with PUMA leading 31 percent of new programes and 48 percent of mortgage-backed securities rated in the period.

"In Australia, strong volumes of mortgage and asset-backed securities issued in the first six months of 1997 have created more efficient markets with increasing depth and liquidity in the trading of these securities," S&P said.

S&P said this was giving issuers greater incentives to tap local capital markets, It said it expected an ever-increasing volume of ratings for the second half of 1997 and forecast new issues to hit a record high.
